newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bourse down in response to market nerves.
newsitem.headline: Irish bourse down in response to market nerves.

text.p: The Irish bourse shed 36.24 points in moderate trading on Tuesday in sympathy with European markets, nervous about a possible rate hike in the U.S. and at continuing fears of a delay in the EMU timetable, dealers said.

"Prices are easier across the board today, reflecting what's happening in international markets," a dealer said. "Weakness in the financials -- down about 1.5 percent -- usually goes in tandem with nervousness on the bonds markets, which we've seen today in response to worries over Wall Street."
Waterford Foods traded at a mark-down of around 20 percent after the company said in a statement it expected 1996 pretax profits to be below current market expectations.
"Waterford is trading at between 75 - 80 pence a share following the profit warning, slightly over 20 percent down on its price," a dealer said.
Waterford blamed "difficult trading conditions" but said pretax profits would not be less than 19.7 million Irish pounds.
Although share prices on the bourse were down overall, dealers said, there was no big pressure on stock in the form of large trade volumes.
Dealers said U.S. CPI data due Wednesday would be closely watched for hints as to the likelihood of a near-term interest rate hike.
"Everybody's watching the U.S., and we're with them, but we're also going to be affected by U.K. confidence in the run-up to the May 1 election," a dealer said.
"Although, I think the probability of a Labour win is already being factored in to the market," the dealer added.
Fears of a delay in EMU continued to dog European markets, dealers added.
By 1730 GMT, the ISEQ index of Irish shares was down 36.24 points or 1.19 percent at 3,010.36.
Among leading financials AIB fell six pence to 439, Bank of Ireland dropped 11 pence to 630, while Irish Life was down 10 pence at 315, and Irish Permanent fell five pence to 615.
Among leading industrials, food stock Avonmore remained unchanged at 250 while CRH fell eight pence to 633. Kerry Group was down five pence to 655.
